criteria.text: Identifies that the Eskdale Systems Ltd contract (Clause 14.2) allows termination on a change of control without consent, that the disclosure against Warranty 6.3 says there is no such provision, and that consent should be obtained as a condition to Closing.

Identifies that the MAC carve-outs (general economic, industry-wide and pandemic changes) contain no 'disproportionate effect' exception, so the Buyer bears those risks even where the Company is disproportionately affected, and recommends adding one.
Identifies that the 4-year SPA non-compete may be unenforceable as wider than reasonably necessary and is inconsistent with the 12-month restriction in the Founder's employment agreement.
Identifies the mismatch between English law / English courts in the SPA and New York law / New York arbitration in the escrow agreement, and the risk of parallel proceedings on escrow claims.
Calculates the working capital shortfall as $620,000 and the adjusted Purchase Price as $99,380,000, identifying that the Seller's funds flow figure of $98,760,000 is wrong.
Flags that the disclosure letter is inconsistent with the material contract on change of control.
Lists the Eskdale Systems Ltd change-of-control consent as a required third-party consent and states it has not been obtained.
Gives a pinpoint citation (document name and section/clause number) for every issue or finding.
